## Description {#details}

<p><a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrsetimplbase">SmallPtrSetImplBase</a> - This is the common code shared among all the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrset">SmallPtrSet&lt;&gt;</a>'s, which is almost everything.</p>


<p><a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrset">SmallPtrSet</a> has two modes, one for small and one for large sets.</p>


<p>Small sets use an array of pointers allocated in the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrset">SmallPtrSet</a> object, which is treated as a simple array of pointers. When a pointer is added to the set, the array is scanned to see if the element already exists, if not the element is 'pushed back' onto the array. If we run out of space in the array, we grow into the 'large set' case. <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallset">SmallSet</a> should be used when the sets are often small. In this case, no memory allocation is used, and only light-weight and cache-efficient scanning is used.</p>


<p>Large sets use a classic exponentially-probed hash table. Empty buckets are represented with an illegal pointer value (-1) to allow null pointers to be inserted. Tombstones are represented with another illegal pointer value (-2), to allow deletion. The hash table is resized when the table is 3/4 or more. When this happens, the table is doubled in size.</p>
